prompt.text:
Your task is to generate a complete research paper using the materials below.
You must produce:
1. A BibTeX bibliography file (references.bib)
2. The full LaTeX paper (template.tex)

Instructions
• Use the research idea and experimental logs to construct a coherent, rigorous ML paper.
• For related work and baselines:
  – Search for and include influential papers published up until 2024-10.
  – Incorporate relevant literature and add the corresponding BibTeX entries to references.bib.
  – Do NOT hallucinate papers or reference keys; all citation entries must be real.
• In the LaTeX paper, cite papers using \cite{} with keys that match exactly with your entries in references.bib.
• Do not fabricate experimental results or make claims unsupported by the logs.

Materials
Here are all the raw research materials to assist with the writing process:

[RESEARCH IDEA]
## Problem Statement
Large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) frequently exhibit societal biases, associating neutral concepts (e.g., "doctor") with specific demographic attributes (e.g., "male"). Existing mitigation strategies, such as adversarial learning or subspace projection, suffer from two critical flaws. First, they rely on scarce, manually annotated datasets (e.g., face-centric datasets), which limits their applicability to diverse, natural imagery. Second, they often aggressively remove attribute information even when it is explicitly requested in the prompt (e.g., ignoring the "female" modifier in "female doctor"), thereby degrading the model's semantic precision and utility in downstream tasks.

## Core Hypothesis
We hypothesize that societal bias in text embeddings can be mitigated without ground-truth labels by enforcing geometric symmetry in the feature space. We posit that an attribute-neutral description (e.g., "a person eating") should map to an embedding that is equidistant from embeddings of its attribute-specific variants (e.g., "a man eating" and "a woman eating"). By training a lightweight correction layer to enforce this equidistance, we can neutralize bias in generic contexts while retaining the model’s ability to represent specific attributes when explicitly prompted.

## Proposed Methodology (High-Level Technical Approach)
We propose a self-supervised, annotation-free framework to train a debiasing adapter for the VLM's text encoder. The approach involves the following "whiteboard" logical flow:

**1. Automated Text Augmentation**
Instead of relying on external labels, we will generate our own training signal using a dictionary-based manipulation of input captions. For a given text containing person-related terms, we will synthesize:
*   **Neutral Set:** Replacing specific terms (e.g., "boy", "aunt") with generic equivalents (e.g., "child", "relative").
*   **Attribute-Specific Set:** Generating variants for every protected group (e.g., substituting "person" with "man", "woman", etc.).

**2. Residual Debiasing Adapter**
We will freeze the original VLM parameters and introduce a shallow Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) on top of the text encoder. This module will learn a residual vector to "correct" the embedding of the neutral text.

**3. Equidistance Optimization Logic**
The core training signal will be a specialized loss function designed to align the *corrected neutral embedding* relative to the *attribute-specific embeddings*.
*   We will compute the cosine similarity between the corrected neutral feature and each of the synthesized specific features.
*   The optimization objective will be to minimize the standard deviation of these similarities. This forces the neutral concept to sit at the geometric "center" of the demographic groups, ensuring no single group is favored.

**4. Semantic Preservation**
To prevent the debiasing layer from destroying the original semantic meaning of the text, we will employ regularization objectives:
*   **Reconstruction:** Constraining the modified feature to remain relatively close to the original feature.
*   **Contrastive Alignment:** Ensuring the modified text feature maintains high compatibility with its corresponding image feature.

## Expected Contribution
*   **Annotation-Independence:** This method eliminates the dependency on ethically fraught and scarce demographic annotation datasets, allowing debiasing to be performed on any large-scale, uncurated image-text corpus.
*   **Selective Neutralization:** Unlike projection methods that "squash" attribute dimensions entirely, this approach preserves attribute information when explicitly stated in the text, ensuring the model can still generate or retrieve specific demographics when prompted.
*   **Model Agnostic Utility:** The proposed lightweight adapter can be applied to existing pre-trained VLMs without requiring expensive retraining of the backbone, facilitating broader adoption in generative and discriminative tasks.

[EXPERIMENTAL LOGS]
## 1. Experimental Setup

We evaluated the proposed method, SANER (Societal Attribute Neutralizer), against existing baselines on discriminative and generative tasks to assess its ability to mitigate societal biases (gender, age, and race) while retaining model utility.

*   **Model Architecture:**
    *   Target Model: CLIP with ViT-B/16 backbone.
    *   Generative Model: Stable Diffusion v2.1 (replacing the original CLIP text encoder with the debiased one).
    *   Debiasing Layer: A multilayer perceptron (MLP) with two linear layers and ReLU activation, appended to the CLIP text encoder. Hidden embedding dimensionality set to 128.
    *   Extension Model: BLIP (used in auxiliary experiments).

*   **Training Configuration:**
    *   **Training Dataset:** A subset of the COCO training set consisting of 170,624 image-caption pairs containing person-related words/phrases. No protected attribute annotations were used.
    *   **Loss Weights:** $\alpha = 1.0$ (debiasing), $\beta = 0.1$ (reconstruction), $\gamma = 0.0001$ (contrastive).
    *   **Hyperparameters:** 5 epochs, batch size 128, learning rate $5 \times 10^{-6}$.
    *   **Hardware:** Single NVIDIA A100 GPU (40GB).
    *   **Training Time:** Approximately five hours.
    *   **Optimization:** Only weights of the debiasing layer were updated; the rest of the model was frozen.

*   **Evaluation Datasets:**
    *   **FairFace:** 10,954 cropped face-centric images with attribute annotations.
    *   **PATA:** 4,934 natural images with a single person and attribute annotations.
    *   **FACET:** Natural images with diverse attribute annotations (used for auxiliary gender bias evaluation).
    *   **ImageNet-1K:** Used for zero-shot image classification accuracy.
    *   **COCO Karpathy Test Set:** Used for evaluating image fidelity and image-text alignment.

*   **Evaluation Metrics:**
    *   **Text-to-Image Retrieval (Bias):** MaxSkew@1000 (measures disparity of attribute distribution in top-k results). Calculated for Adjectives, Occupations, and Activities. Lower is better.
    *   **Text-to-Image Retrieval (Utility):** Top-1 Accuracy (Zero-shot classification on ImageNet-1K).
    *   **Text-to-Image Generation (Bias):** Statistical Parity (SP). Measures disparity of attribute groups in generated images. Lower is better.
    *   **Text-to-Image Generation (Attribute Retention):** Accuracy (ratio of images containing the specific gender requested in the prompt). Higher is better.
    *   **Text-to-Image Generation (Quality):** FID (Fidelity) and CLIPScore (Image-Text Alignment).

*   **Baselines Compared:**
    *   **Original:** Original CLIP (Radford et al., 2021) or Stable Diffusion.
    *   **Prompt:** Prompt tuning-based debiasing (Berg et al., 2022).
    *   **Projection:** Projection-based debiasing (Chuang et al., 2023).

## 3. Qualitative Observations

*   **Gender Bias Mitigation:** We observed that SANER consistently achieved the lowest MaxSkew scores across FairFace, PATA, and FACET datasets for Adjectives, Occupations, and Activities, indicating superior debiasing capability compared to baselines.
*   **Cross-Domain Consistency:** Unlike Prompt tuning, which failed to mitigate activity bias on FairFace (increasing it from 19.5 to 20.0), SANER effectively reduced bias across both face-centric (FairFace) and natural image (PATA) domains.
*   **Race and Age Mitigation:** We found that SANER successfully mitigated racial and age biases. For instance, Projection-based debiasing amplified racial bias in occupations (57.4 to 75.3), whereas SANER reduced it (to 45.7).
*   **Zero-Shot Performance:** We verified that applying SANER maintained the zero-shot classification performance of the original CLIP on ImageNet (65.2% vs 65.4%), whereas Prompt tuning caused a slight degradation (64.1%).
*   **Text-to-Image Generation (Gender Balance):** Qualitative analysis of generated images for gender-neutral prompts (e.g., "A photo of a designer", "A photo of a teacher") showed that Original SD and Projection-based methods predominantly generated males. In contrast, SANER produced a more balanced gender distribution.
*   **Attribute Retention (Explicit Prompts):** When using prompts with explicit gender attributes (e.g., "A photo of a female doctor", "A photo of a male musician"):
    *   Projection-based methods frequently ignored the attribute, generating males for "female doctor" and females for "male musician" (Accuracy drops to 0.58 and 0.79 respectively).
    *   SANER retained the attribute information perfectly (Accuracy 1.00), generating images consistent with the text prompt.
*   **Ablation Findings (Losses):** We observed that removing regularization losses significantly degraded zero-shot classification (dropping to 58.8%). Using Contrastive loss alone resulted in higher bias (MaxSkew) compared to using no regularization. The combination of Reconstruction and Contrastive losses yielded the optimal balance of debiasing and performance retention.
*   **Ablation Findings (Data Size):** We noted a trend where increasing the size of the training dataset (from 50% to 100% of the COCO subset) progressively reduced gender bias scores.
*   **Generation Quality:** We evaluated image fidelity and alignment on the COCO Karpathy test set. SANER achieved FID (28.7) and CLIPScore (31.0) comparable to the original Stable Diffusion (FID 28.1, CLIPScore 31.2), confirming that debiasing did not compromise generation quality.
*   **Model Agnosticism:** We confirmed that SANER is effective on other VLMs; experiments on BLIP showed SANER reduced bias compared to the original BLIP and Projection baselines.

Role: Senior AI Researcher and Academic Writer.
Objective: Complete a machine learning research paper by filling in missing sections of a provided LaTeX template and generating a corresponding bibliography file. You must produce a scientifically sound, well-structured paper suitable for submission to a top-tier ML conference.

Inputs
You will receive the following materials:
• idea.md: Detailed description of the proposed method and technical ideas.
• experimental_log.md: Raw experimental results and observations used to construct tables, figures, and analysis.
• conference_guidelines.md: Formatting and stylistic requirements for the target conference.
• figures_list: A list of figures that may be referenced in the paper.

Conference Guidelines
# ICLR 2025 Paper Writing Guidelines

Below are the instructions to help you with the LaTeX paper writing process for ICLR 2025.

## General Setup
* **Document Class:** `\documentclass{article}`
* **Required Packages:**
    ```latex
    \usepackage{iclr2025_conference,times}
    \usepackage{hyperref}
    \usepackage{url}
    % Optional but recommended for math
    \input{math_commands.tex}
    ```
* **Style Files:** You must use `iclr2025_conference.sty` and `iclr2025_conference.bst`.

## Anonymity (Crucial)
* ICLR is double-blind. **Do not** include real author names or affiliations in the submission version, use "Ambitious AI Researcher" instead.
* Use the third person when citing your own prior work (e.g., "Earlier work by Smalle (2024)..." instead of "In our earlier work...").
* You may post your paper on arXiv, but do not explicitly refer to the arXiv version in the paper to maintain anonymity.

## Paper Length
* **Main Text:** Strict upper limit of **10 pages**.
* **Citations:** Unlimited additional pages.
* **Ethics & Reproducibility Statements:** Optional. Do not count toward the page limit (max 1 page each).
* **Acknowledgments:** Do not count toward the page limit.

## Abstract
The abstract must be limited to **one paragraph**.
* **Margins:** Indented 1/2 inch (3 picas) on both left and right-hand margins.
* **Font:** 10-point type, vertical spacing of 11-points.
* **Title:** The word `\textsc{Abstract}` must be centered, in small caps, and in point size 12.
* **Spacing:** Two line spaces precede the abstract.

## Formatting Your Paper
The text must be confined within a rectangle 5.5 inches (33 picas) wide and 9 inches (54 picas) long. The left margin is 1.5 inch (9 picas).
* **Font:** Times New Roman (via `times` package) is preferred.
* **Size:** 10-point type with 11-point vertical spacing.
* **Paragraphs:** Separated by 1/2 line space, with **no indentation**.
* **Paper Title:** 17-point, small caps, left-aligned.

### Headings
* **First Level:** Small caps (`\textsc`), flush left, 12-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.
* **Second Level:** Small caps, flush left, 10-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.
* **Third Level:** Small caps, flush left, 10-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.

## Citations and References
Use the `natbib` package (loaded automatically by the style file).
* **Narrative citation:** Use `\citet{Gomu2024}` $\rightarrow$ "Gomu et al. (2024)".
* **Parenthetical citation:** Use `\citep{Gomu2024}` $\rightarrow$ "(Gomu et al., 2024)".
* **Bibliography:**
    ```latex
    \bibliography{references}
    \bibliographystyle{iclr2025_conference}
    ```

## Figures and Tables
* All artwork must be neat, clean, and legible.
* **Captions:** Lower case (except for first word and proper nouns).
* **Placement:**
    * **Figures:** Caption appears **after** (below) the figure.
    * **Tables:** Caption appears **before** (above) the table.

### Example Code for Figures

```latex
\\ \hline \\

Axon             &Output terminal \\
Soma             &Cell body (contains cell nucleus) \\
\end{tabular}

\end{table}
```

## Math Notation
* ICLR encourages standardized notation using `\input{math_commands.tex}` (based on the Deep Learning book notation).
* Variables: Italics ($a$, $\va$, $\mA$).
* Random Variables: Roman ($P(\ra)$).
* Sets: Blackboard bold ($\R$, $\sA$).
* Functions: Standard LaTeX ($f(\vx)$).

## Optional Statements
These should appear at the end of the main text, before references.
1.  **Ethics Statement:** (Optional, max 1 page) Address potential concerns (human subjects, sensitive data, bias, etc.).
2.  **Reproducibility Statement:** (Optional, max 1 page) Reference code, proofs, or data processing steps to ensure reproducibility.

## Important Rules
* **Formatting:** Do not modify the width or length of the text rectangle or font sizes.
* **Line Numbers:** Do not refer to line numbers in your text (the style file adds them automatically for review).
* **Appendix:** You may include an appendix at the very end of the main PDF (after references). Use `\appendix` to start this section.
* **Figures Directory:** For consistent compilation, all figures will reside in the `figures` directory. Always include the `figures/` prefix in your `\includegraphics` command (e.g., `figures/figure_1.pdf`).
* **Author Information:** Always use the following author information placeholder in your writeup:
    * Ambitious AI Researcher, AI Research Institute, 123 AI Avenue, ML City, researcher@institute.ai

Critical Constraints
1. Scientific Integrity
• All reported experimental results MUST match the provided experimental logs.
• Never fabricate results, numbers, baselines, datasets, or metrics.
• If results are weak, negative, or inconclusive, report them honestly and discuss possible explanations.
2. Literature Cutoff Rule
You must behave as if the current date is: 2024-10. Do NOT cite or discuss papers published after this date.
3. Page Limit
The main paper is limited to 10 pages (including figures and tables but excluding references and appendices). Use space efficiently while remaining concise.
4. Template Compliance
• Do not modify the overall LaTeX style or document structure mandated by the conference template.
• References must be handled through a references.bib file.
• Use standard LaTeX citation commands (e.g., \cite{}). Make sure you ONLY cite keys that exist in your generated BibTeX code block.

Section Guidelines
• Title: Concise, descriptive, and memorable. Preferably under two lines.
• Abstract: A single, compelling paragraph summarizing the problem context, proposed approach, key results, and main takeaway.
• Introduction: Introduce the problem and motivate its importance. Provide necessary background context. Clearly summarize the paper's core contributions.
• Related Work: Discuss prior work addressing similar or related problems. Detail the relationship between existing literature and the current approach. Cite relevant baselines and influential papers published before 2024-10.
• Methodology: Clearly and pedantically describe the proposed method. Provide sufficient technical depth for full reproducibility. Use equations, figures, and structured explanations when appropriate.
• Experiments: Detail the empirical setup (datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and implementation details). Present results faithfully based on the experimental logs. Ensure any figures located in the figures/ directory are seamlessly integrated and referenced in text.
• Conclusion: Summarize the main findings and contributions. Briefly and realistically discuss limitations and potential future directions.
• Appendix (optional): Include supplementary details that do not fit within the main page limit.

LaTeX Quality Requirements
Ensure the generated LaTeX compiles flawlessly out-of-the-box. Avoid common issues such as:
• Unmatched braces or unclosed math environments.
• Duplicate labels.
• Unescaped special characters (e.g., & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ \).
All referenced figures must exist in the provided list.

Output Format

references.text:
## Problem Statement
Large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) effectively encode multi-modal representations but inadvertently capture and amplify societal biases (e.g., regarding gender, age, and race) present in their massive training corpora. While existing mitigation strategies—such as adversarial learning or test-time projection—attempt to reduce these biases, they suffer from two critical technical limitations.

First, existing methods often incur a **loss of explicit attribute information**. By aggressively decorrelating features from protected attributes or squashing attribute-related subspaces, these methods fail to distinguish between biased associations and explicit user intent (e.g., a prompt for a "female doctor" is neutralized to a generic "doctor," ignoring the user's specification). Second, current adversarial approaches rely heavily on **attribute-annotated datasets** (e.g., face-centric datasets with gender labels). These datasets are scarce, ethically complex to curate, and lack the domain diversity required to fine-tune general-purpose VLMs effectively. We address the need for a debiasing framework that functions on arbitrary, unannotated image-text pairs while preserving semantic fidelity when attributes are explicitly invoked.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose a novel, lightweight debiasing framework titled **SANER (Societal Attribute Neutralizer)**. Our core hypothesis is that we can disentangle societal bias from semantic content without attribute labels by enforcing a geometric constraint in the feature space: the embedding of an **attribute-neutral** description should be equidistant to the embeddings of its **attribute-specific** variations.

By training a residual debiasing layer (a Multilayer Perceptron) to satisfy this equidistance constraint, we hypothesize that:
1.  We can remove bias from neutral prompts (where bias is harmful).
2.  We can retain attribute information in explicit prompts (where the attribute is semantically necessary).
3.  We can train this system using only text augmentation on standard image-text datasets, eliminating the need for protected attribute annotations.

## Proposed Methodology (Detailed Technical Approach)

We will implement a post-hoc debiasing mechanism for the text encoder of a pre-trained VLM (specifically CLIP). The methodology consists of attribute neutralization, feature modification via a learnable layer, and a composite loss function centered on an annotation-free debiasing objective.

### 1. Notation and Problem Setup
Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote a dataset of image-text pairs $(v, t)$, where $v$ is an image and $t$ is a text description. We assume no protected attribute annotations are provided. Let $f_{\mathrm{t}}(t) \in \mathbb{R}^{K}$ and $f_{\mathrm{v}}(v) \in \mathbb{R}^{K}$ denote the frozen, pre-trained text and image encoders, respectively.

### 2. Text Augmentation Strategy
To facilitate annotation-free training, we will mechanically generate variations of the input text $t$:
*   **Attribute Neutralization ($\xi_{\mathrm{n}}$):** We define a function $\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t)$ that identifies attribute-specific terms (e.g., "woman", "man", "young", "old") and replaces them with attribute-neutral terms (e.g., "person"). For example, "A woman is eating" becomes "A person is eating".
*   **Attribute Specification ($\xi_{g}$):** For a protected attribute set $\mathcal{A}$ (e.g., $\{\mathtt{female}, \mathtt{male}\}$), we define $\xi_{g}(t)$ which generates specific descriptions for each group $g \in \mathcal{A}$.

### 3. Feature Modification Architecture
We will introduce a learnable debiasing layer $r$, modeled as a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) consisting of two linear layers with ReLU activation. The hidden embedding dimensionality will be set to 128.

This layer operates as a residual correction to the original CLIP text embeddings. For a neutralized text input $\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t)$, the debiased feature vector $h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))$ is defined as:
$$ h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t)) = z(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t)) + r(z(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))) $$
where $z(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t)) = f_{\mathrm{t}}(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))$ is the original frozen CLIP embedding of the neutralized text.

### 4. Attribute Annotation-Free Debiasing Loss
The core of our proposal is the objective function. We aim to position the debiased neutral embedding $h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))$ such that it does not favor any specific attribute group $g$.

We define the cosine similarity $s_{g}(t)$ between the *debiased neutral* feature and the *original specific* feature for group $g$:
$$ s_{g}(t) = \frac{h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))^{\top} f_{\mathrm{t}}(\xi_{g}(t))}{\|h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))\| \|f_{\mathrm{t}}(\xi_{g}(t))\|} $$

To ensure impartiality, $h(\xi_{\mathrm{n}}(t))$ must be equidistant to all $f_{\mathrm{t}}(\xi_{g}(t))$. We formulate the debiasing loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{deb}}$ as the standard deviation of these similarities:
$$ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{deb}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}|} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{D}}(s_{g}(t) - \bar{s}(t))^{2}} $$
where $\bar{s}(t) = \sum_{g \in \mathcal{A}} s_{g}(t) / |\mathcal{A}|$ is the mean similarity. Minimizing this standard deviation enforces the equidistance constraint.

### 5. Regularization via Reconstruction and Contrastive Losses
To prevent the debiasing layer from destroying semantic utility or image-text alignment, we will incorporate two regularization terms using the original (non-neutralized) text $t$:

*   **Reconstruction Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{recon}}$):** Minimizes the Mean Squared Error (MSE) between the original feature and the modified feature to preserve semantics.
    $$ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{recon}} = \| f_{\mathrm{t}}(t) - h(t) \|^2 $$
*   **Contrastive Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cont}}$):** Maintains the alignment between the image $v$ and the modified text feature. We minimize the negative log-likelihood of the correct image-text pairs against negative samples, consistent with the original CLIP training objective.

### 6. Total Optimization Objective
The final loss function $\mathcal{L}$ is a weighted sum of the three components:
$$ \mathcal{L} = \alpha \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{deb}} + \beta \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{recon}} + \gamma \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cont}} $$
We propose the following hyperparameter configuration based on preliminary theoretical analysis: $\alpha = 1.0$, $\beta = 0.1$, and $\gamma = 0.0001$. During inference, the learned layer $r$ is applied to any input text feature to produce the final representation.

## Expected Contribution
This project aims to deliver a theoretically sound and practically robust solution to bias in VLMs.
1.  **Annotation Independence:** By relying on text augmentation rather than labeled images, we enable debiasing using massive, diverse, uncurated datasets (e.g., COCO) rather than limited face databases.
2.  **Semantic Preservation:** Unlike projection methods that squash attribute dimensions entirely, our residual architecture allows the model to retain attribute information when explicitly prompted (e.g., generating a "female doctor" correctly) while neutralizing bias in ambiguous contexts.
3.  **Model Compatibility:** The proposed method does not require retraining the heavy backbone (CLIP) and introduces negligible computational overhead during inference, making it highly deployable.

notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].

preinstalled.zh: python:3.11 bookworm；上游代码按 PYTHONPATH 使用；pdflatex + bibtex；CPU 版 PyTorch 和 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、pandas、matplotlib 等（constraints.txt 固定）
preinstalled.en: python:3.11 bookworm; upstream code via PYTHONPATH; pdflatex + bibtex; CPU PyTorch with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib and more (pinned by constraints.txt)

notes.model: claude-opus-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools, no thinking parameter); ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. Generated experiments run as a plain subprocess in the container.
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (for example 4096) is shared with the thinking tokens, so long outputs can still be cut short.
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE and RWE_EFFORT switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s, refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md verbatim with whitespace collapsed. Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: Generated experiment code inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
